ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the attached figure, the vertical axis is labeled h(t), and the horizontal axis is t. The curve starts from the black dot at t=0, the amplitude is labeled 1, and then only on the t>0 side it decays to the right in exponential form and approaches 0, labeled in the figure as e^{-t}. Therefore the impulse response of this system can be read as the causal signal h(t)=e^{-t}ε(t). Then reason: the step response is the response of the system to the unit step input; for an LTI system, the step response equals the integral of the impulse response from -∞ to t, namely s(t)=∫_{-∞}^{t}h(τ)dτ. Since h(τ)=0 (τ<0), when t<0, s(t)=0; when t≥0, s(t)=∫_0^t e^{-τ}dτ=1-e^{-t}. Combining causality, obtain s(t)=(1-e^{-t})ε(t).

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the plotted h(t) is a causal decaying exponential starting at 1 at t=0, hence infer h(t)=e^{-t}ε(t). From the question text, the requested quantity is the step response. Use the LTI relation step response = integral of impulse response: s(t)=∫_{-∞}^{t}h(τ)dτ. Evaluate s(t)=∫_0^t e^{-τ}dτ=1-e^{-t} for t≥0, and attach ε(t) for causality, giving (1-e^{-t})ε(t).
